review: Seven exception-field raw IR deltas were examined in full against the extracted fix and exact test-source hashes. No unexplained semantic or layout changes. Additional strings/declarations, register numbering and TBAA changes follow directly from the new guarded reads and shared layout. This review classifies the retained IR; execution proof is recorded separately.

cases.rationale: Existing assignment flag is preserved. Base.show now tests the concrete ExcClass against Sub and loads the current mutable Sub.label default when the instance flag is clear. The assigned instance value still takes precedence. Missing Base and Plain fields retain the AttributeError path and dynamic class name.

hasattr combines the existing assignment flag with concrete Sub or Deep membership, without depending on a preceding field read. Missing Base and Plain fields remain false; any base-typed assignment sets the flag.

The exception base and subclass now share an i1 assignment flag at offset 32, and both numeric identity-box slots move consistently to offset 40. The read selects the current Sub.value and its class-global .box address together; assigned values select the instance box. Base initialization and base-typed writes set the shared flag. TBAA offsets agree with the common prefix.

The exception base gains the same assignment flag as Sub. Dynamic fallback selection, instance storage, and returns preserve the entire promoting-integer {i64, ptr} value. Both words remain together through class-default and assigned-instance paths; initialization and base-typed writes set the flag.

label and count assignment bits become shared base-prefix members. Base methods, Base parameters, and except-Base reads select the current Sub defaults for concrete Sub or Deep objects until assignment. hasattr uses the same membership-or-flag criterion. The two field values and flags remain distinct, constructor/instance writes establish ownership, and TBAA tracks the shared layout.

The shared label flag guards concrete-class default selection. Sub, Deep and Grand select the Sub.label global; Other selects its independently mutable Other.label global. Instance values win once assigned. Both Base.show and the Base-typed view use this selection; base initialization and assignment set the common flag.

The base layout now includes the flag already read through Sub. Both Base.__init__ and Base-typed relabel set that shared flag after storing the value, so assigned instances stop using the class default. The obsolete Sub-only flag TBAA node is replaced by the common Base prefix.
